fieldMarks: Stout toad-like amphibian, 5.6-8.8 cm; bright green-yellow to brown-yellow with dark green, brown or black mottling (more extensive in females), white belly.
Vertically elliptical pupil in bright light and a single hard, black, sickle-shaped spade on each hind foot.
Parotoid glands present but indistinct; skin with many small warts.
Breeding male has dark patches on the inner three digits and a large, rounded vocal sac; call is a harsh lamb- or goat-like bleat lasting 0.5-1 s.
behavior: Nocturnal; spends most of its time underground in burrows dug backwards with the hind spades, and surfaces after heavy rains.
Breeds explosively after heavy spring or summer rains, often in a single night, in temporary pools; eggs hatch within about 36 hours and metamorphosis takes about 1-2 weeks if pools persist.
Eats mostly insects and other small terrestrial arthropods; can go about ten months without feeding while dormant.
habitat: Arid and semi-arid shrublands, shortgrass plains, mesquite savanna, creosote-bush desert, thornforest and cultivated areas; eggs are attached to vegetation in shallow rain pools.
range: Southwestern United States (Arizona, California, Colorado, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas) into northern Mexico and Baja California; not found in Canada.
